---
title: Biometric Signing
---

In enforced mode a block is signed by a passkey: a WebAuthn credential whose private key lives in
the signer's authenticator (the Secure Enclave behind Touch ID, Windows Hello, a YubiKey Bio) and
which signs only after the authenticator has verified the user. This page covers how a passkey is
enrolled and bound to a signer, how a block is signed with it, what the registry attests about the
key, and what a signature does not prove.


## How Signing Works

`sib sign` with a passkey enrolled builds the header, prints the canonical text and the terms, and
starts a small web app on `http://localhost:7391`. It opens the sign page in the default browser
and waits:

![The sign page: the canonical text in a monospace box, the signer, key, expiry, audience and
nonce, and one button.](../../project/plans/findings/images/phase-2/sign-before.png){width=80%}

The page shows the canonical instruction, the signer, the key, the expiry, the audience and the
nonce, and nothing else. That is the what-you-see-is-what-you-sign surface. The button calls
`navigator.credentials.get` with `userVerification: "required"` and a challenge computed by the
command before the page opened:

```text
challenge = SHA-256( BASE64URL(signing header) || "." || canonical instruction )
```

The signing header is the block's header without the three assertion fields described below,
because they are not known until the authenticator has signed. The browser prompts for Touch ID
(or the platform's equivalent), the authenticator signs, and the page posts the assertion back to
the command. The command runs the [verifier](verifier.qmd) over the result and writes the block
only when the status is `verified`; a failing status is printed instead, and no block is written.

```bash
sib sign --signer alice@example.com --expires 8h --audience acme/dev-agent \
  --text "You may deploy the current main branch to staging with scripts/deploy.sh staging whenever the test suite passes." \
  --out block.txt
```

```text
About to sign (canonical form):
  You may deploy the current main branch to staging with scripts/deploy.sh staging whenever the test suite passes.
  signer=alice@example.com kid=alice@example.com#passkey-9188 expires=2026-10-05T19:45:21Z audience=acme/dev-agent canon=text/1 mode=enforced
Opening http://localhost:7391/sign/xVOorN3_EUxrNGbBsgSAOAA7dRAzbTaD
signed with alice@example.com#passkey-9188 in 0.5 s
wrote block.txt
```

The resulting block has `alg: ES256-webauthn` and `mode: enforced` in its header, and carries the
assertion in three header fields: `credentialId`, `authenticatorData` and `clientDataJSON`, all
base64url. The signature segment is the ECDSA P-256 signature the authenticator returned, which
covers `authenticatorData` and the hash of `clientDataJSON`; `clientDataJSON` carries the
challenge, which is the hash of the header and the instruction. That is the chain from the
signer's fingerprint to the text. The [Block Format](../../spec/format.qmd#webauthn-assertion)
page has a complete example.

Every signing request has a one-time token in its URL. The page works once, for the payload the
command created; a stale tab cannot sign a different payload.

::: {.callout-note}
A passkey-signed block needs an audience. Enforced-mode verifiers refuse a block with no `aud`,
so `sib sign` refuses to create one.
:::


## Enrollment

Enrollment binds a passkey to a signer id:

```bash
sib enroll --signer alice@example.com
```

The command opens the enroll page, which calls `navigator.credentials.create` with user
verification required, a platform authenticator requested, a discoverable credential preferred
and `attestation: "direct"`:

![The enroll page after a successful enrollment, reporting the authenticator and the attestation
result.](../../project/plans/findings/images/phase-2/enroll-after.png){width=80%}

The response is verified with [py_webauthn](https://github.com/duo-labs/py_webauthn): the
challenge, the origin and the RP ID must match, the user must have been verified, and the
attestation statement is checked as far as a root certificate allows (next section). Only ES256
credentials are offered to the authenticator, since that is the algorithm `ES256-webauthn`
names. The command then writes the registry entry and prints what it recorded:

```text
enrolled alice@example.com#passkey-9188 for alice@example.com in /Users/alice/.sib/registry.json (enforced mode, authenticator 01020304-0506-0708-0102-030405060708, attestation packed not verified)
warning: authenticator 01020304-0506-0708-0102-030405060708 is not on the biometric-capable allowlist; blocks signed with alice@example.com#passkey-9188 fail with authenticator_not_allowed until it is added under allowed_aaguids in /Users/alice/.sib/registry.json
attestation_verified=false: the AAGUID is the authenticator's own claim; hardware backing is an enrollment assumption for this key
```

The key id follows the convention `<signer>#passkey-<first two bytes of the credential id>`;
`--kid` overrides it. Each enrollment uses a fresh WebAuthn user handle, because an authenticator
that sees a user handle it already holds for this site replaces the earlier passkey, which would
orphan the key enrolled under the earlier `kid`. Credentials already enrolled for the signer are
excluded, so the same authenticator is not enrolled twice.

Two environment variables shape enrollment:

`SIB_REQUIRE_ATTESTATION`
: When set to `1`, an enrollment whose attestation cannot be verified is refused. Off by default:
  Apple passkeys usually carry no attestation, and the demo accepts them and says so.

`SIB_ATTESTATION_ROOTS`
: A directory of PEM root certificates. Attestation statements in the `packed`, `tpm` and
  `fido-u2f` formats are chained to these roots; without them, a chain in those formats is
  recorded but counts as unverified. Apple's WebAuthn root is bundled, so the `apple` format
  needs nothing here.


## What the Registry Attests

The entry for a passkey:

```json
{
  "kid": "alice@example.com#passkey-9188",
  "alg": "ES256-webauthn",
  "public_key": "pQECAyYgASFYIAme6lzACHBimeQ_-XoqnWCJGkWnolTu63bWExx4t1mZIlggf_dOOJAncBQ8B9jE1koWCovF_qJejGQv_fBEm2QL1oY",
  "mode": "enforced",
  "enrolled_at": "2026-10-05T11:45:20Z",
  "attestation_verified": false,
  "attestation": {"format": "packed", "x5c_present": true, "roots": null},
  "revoked": false,
  "credential_id": "kYjC6VVDjNGdsK9jHcPPariB-AUWC8KDxWLVH-Vp9p4",
  "aaguid": "01020304-0506-0708-0102-030405060708",
  "sign_count": 1,
  "origins": ["http://localhost:7391"],
  "rp_id": "localhost",
  "user_verified_at_enrollment": true,
  "transports": ["internal"]
}
```

Each field answers a different question, and they do not all carry the same weight:

`public_key`, `credential_id`
: What the verifier needs: the COSE-encoded P-256 public key and the credential the assertion
  must come from. These are cryptographically bound to every signature.

`attestation_verified`
: `true` only when the attestation statement carried a certificate chain and a root for its
  format was available to check it against. Then the authenticator's make and model are vouched
  for by its vendor. `false` means the AAGUID below is the authenticator's own claim: with
  attestation `none` (what iCloud Keychain passkeys return) or a chain with no configured root,
  the WebAuthn specification gives no provenance guarantee. The manifest carries this flag on
  every span so a classifier policy can require it.

`aaguid`
: The authenticator model identifier. Policy input for the allowlist below; proof of nothing by
  itself.

`origins`, `rp_id`
: Where the key may be used. An assertion made on another web origin, or for another RP ID, is
  refused. A block signed on one laptop verifies elsewhere only if the verifier's registry entry
  lists that origin; the Phase 3 specification revisits this.

`sign_count`
: The authenticator's signature counter at enrollment. Recorded, not enforced: Apple passkeys
  report zero and never increment it.

`user_verified_at_enrollment`, `uvm`
: Whether the UV flag was set when the passkey was created, and the user-verification-method
  extension result when the browser supplied one. Most browsers do not.

::: {.callout-warning}
The registry proves possession of a key by whoever enrolled it under a signer id. It does not
prove that the signer id belongs to the person at the keyboard; that binding is an enrollment
procedure (someone checks the id before running `sib enroll`), and the external directory that
would make it auditable is out of scope.
:::


## What User Verification Does Not Prove

The verifier requires the assertion's UV flag, so a block is never produced without the
authenticator verifying the user. Three limits remain, and they are stated here rather than
hidden:

User verification is not biometric verification
: WebAuthn's UV flag is set by a PIN or a password as readily as by a fingerprint. On macOS,
  after a few failed Touch ID attempts the system offers the login password, and the resulting
  assertion is indistinguishable. No field in the assertion names the method; the `uvm`
  extension that would is poorly supported. The project plan's requirement SG-2 asks for
  biometric verification specifically, and the assertion cannot deliver it.

The allowlist is policy
: To narrow the gap, the verifier accepts only authenticators whose AAGUID is on a list of
  models known to verify users biometrically (`sib.keys_webauthn.DEFAULT_ALLOWED_AAGUIDS`: Apple
  Passwords, iCloud Keychain (Managed), Chrome on Mac, Windows Hello, and every YubiKey Bio
  model). A registry adds entries under `allowed_aaguids`, or with
  [`sib allow-authenticator`](../basics/cli.qmd#allow-authenticator). The list was audited on
  19 October 2026 against `passkeydeveloper/passkey-authenticator-aaguids`, whose `aaguid.json`
  names the platform providers and whose FIDO MDS derived `combined_aaguid.json` names the
  hardware models; re-audit before an enforced deployment relies on it, because vendors add
  models and rename them. It is only as strong as the attestation behind the AAGUID: an
  authenticator with attestation `none` can report any AAGUID it likes. The all-zero AAGUID, which Apple's `apple` attestation reports, is
  accepted only for a key whose attestation was verified, since many authenticators zero the
  field under attestation `none`.

Passkeys sync
: An iCloud Keychain passkey exists on every device signed in to the signer's Apple account. The
  key is hardware-bound on each of them, but "the key is on one laptop" does not hold.

A password manager may answer instead
: A manager's browser extension can capture the WebAuthn prompt and create the passkey in its own
  vault rather than the platform authenticator. The credential is then a synced secret in software,
  bound to no device, and it reports its own AAGUID with attestation `none`. Such models are
  deliberately absent from the default allowlist, so enrollment succeeds and both signing and
  verification then fail with `authenticator_not_allowed`, naming the AAGUID. `--browser` selects a
  browser whose prompt the platform answers; `sib allow-authenticator` accepts one on purpose.

If the allowlist is judged insufficient, the options are enterprise attestation to pin
authenticator models, or a Secure Enclave key created with a biometry-only access-control flag
through a small native helper, which is macOS-only. Both are raised as specification questions
for Phase 3. The [threat model](../deep-dives/threat-model.qmd) carries the residual gap.

A browser with `userVerification: "required"` will not return an assertion with UV clear; it
fails the ceremony instead. The `uv_not_performed` status therefore catches a crafted assertion
presented directly to the verifier, not a browser flow, and that is what the tests and the
conformance vectors exercise.


## Enforced Mode

Once any passkey is enrolled in the registry, the verifier's default mode is `enforced`:
`sib verify`, the hooks and the manifest all switch without configuration. In enforced mode:

- A dev-mode block or key is `dev_key_in_enforced_mode` and confers nothing.

- A block with no audience is `audience_mismatch`.

- No dev-mode warning prints.

`SIB_MODE=dev` overrides the default; both paths then verify and the warning prints on every
operation. `SIB_MODE=enforced` forces enforced mode before a passkey exists. `sib sign --dev`
signs with a dev key even when a passkey is enrolled, and `sib verify --dev` verifies in dev mode.


## Recording a Real Assertion for the Tests

The test suite signs with a software authenticator so every path runs in CI. One test,
`test_recorded_real_assertion`, checks a block signed by a real passkey and is skipped until the
fixture exists. To record one on a laptop with Touch ID:

1. Enroll and sign as above, into a scratch `SIB_HOME`, writing the block to `block.txt`.

2. Write `tests/fixtures/webauthn/real_assertion.json`:

   ```json
   {
     "block": "<the contents of block.txt>",
     "registry": <the contents of $SIB_HOME/registry.json>,
     "now": "<an RFC 3339 UTC time inside the block's validity window>",
     "audience": "acme/dev-agent",
     "tamper": ["to staging", "to production"]
   }
   ```

   `tamper` names a substitution the test applies to the block, which must then fail with
   `invalid_signature`.

3. Run `just test`; the test now runs.

The registry in the fixture must list the authenticator's AAGUID under `allowed_aaguids` when it
is not on the built-in list.


## Environment

`SIB_BROWSER`
: The browser to open the enroll and sign pages in: a name the Python `webbrowser` module knows
  (`safari`, `chrome`, `firefox`) or a command the URL is appended to (`open -a Safari`). Unset,
  the system default browser opens the page. `--browser` on `sib enroll` and `sib sign` overrides
  it for one command. Use it when the default browser has no passkey support, or when a password
  manager's extension captures the passkey prompt (1Password, for instance, creates the passkey in
  its own vault, which is not on the biometric-capable allowlist).

`SIB_WEBAUTHN_PORT`
: The port of the local app (default `7391`). The origin `http://localhost:<port>` is recorded
  in the registry at enrollment, so a key enrolled on one port verifies assertions from that port
  only.

`SIB_REQUIRE_ATTESTATION`, `SIB_ATTESTATION_ROOTS`
: See [Enrollment](#enrollment).

`SIB_MODE`
: See [Enforced Mode](#enforced-mode).
